problems.problem: No studio equipment is visible, but the backdrop is a generic warm ivory gradient with a soft horizontal tonal transition behind the bottle base. Unlike the Dior reference's satin-lit gold environment or Jo Malone's contextual soft set, this reads as an undifferentiated empty sweep with no material character, weakening the luxury concept.

The single bottle occupies 0.5903 of canvas height (in hero range) and sits correctly at base_y 1245 with bottom margin within limits; contact detail crop confirms a real contact line with a soft occlusion shadow at the base, so physical integration is sound. However, the frame is a purely symmetric, inert stack: logo, title, bottle, subtitle all dead-center with no secondary visual element or depth cue, which reads generic next to the layered reference compositions.

Title and logo are clean Times with no product overlap (text_product_overlap all false), but the subtitle 'EAU DE PARFUM' at size 24 sits isolated under the bottle with weak presence, and title/brand/subtitle share one size logic with no contrast strategy, reducing editorial polish.

References build atmosphere (gold satin, soft flesh-toned light, contextual props) around the product. This poster's flat ivory field and single centered object fail to close that quality gap; lighting on the bottle is bright frontal and the background does not echo or extend it.

changes.value: Empty warm ivory seamless studio environment, polished ivory floor plane meeting a softly lit wall in a seamless curve, broad diffused frontal light with a subtle warm glow pooling behind the central space, faint reflective sheen on the floor beneath the open center, gentle low-contrast falloff at the corners, no objects, no horizon edge
